title: POV: Why Dogs Lick You: Penn Vet Says It's Not a Kiss 🐶 (Things Living In Your House)
description:
Why do dogs lick you? POV: you're Meatball, and your dog is licking your face. A University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine handout says a dog licking a person or another dog is not a "kiss." It is a greeting behavior, but if a dog licks someone repeatedly, he may be anxious about that dog or person. Lip licking is a different signal: Penn Vet lists it as anxiety about a situation or interaction, and AAHA and Texas A&M also list lip licking among nervous or distress signs. A Tufts veterinary behaviorist says an anxious dog may also appear extra friendly and lick a face. Penn Vet also says dogs do not kiss, and they may be frightened by kissing.

#whydodogslickyou #doglicking #dogbehavior #dogsoftiktok #dogfacts

Sources: University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine, Dog Body Language Basics, https://www.vet.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/dogbodylanguagebasics-pdf.pdf ; Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine at Tufts University, Anxiety in Dogs, https://vet.tufts.edu/news-events/news/anxiety-dogs ; AAHA, Common Signs of Anxiety/Distress, https://www.aaha.org/resources/2015-aaha-canine-and-feline-behavior-management-guidelines/common-signs-of-anxietydistress/ ; Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine, Understanding Your Dog's Body Language, https://stories.tamu.edu/news/2025/03/13/understanding-your-dogs-body-language-a-guide-to-canine-communication/ .
